event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: FDX continues to frame the COVID-19 pandemic and future public-health crises as material, but now largely prospective, enterprise-wide threats.  The 2024 filing no longer cites specific dollar impacts; instead management stresses the pandemic’s enduring ability to disrupt demand profiles, supply-chain fluidity, labor availability, cost structure and regulatory posture.  The language is broad and conditional ("could," "may"), signalling that the most acute financial pain has passed, yet the company still sees a meaningful possibility of renewed volatility—especially through new variants, travel or lockdown restrictions, and heightened compliance costs.  These statements therefore represent forward-looking, unquantified risk disclosures rather than confirmations of current impairment.  Given that the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic more than four years ago (March 2020) and the filing date is July 2024, the Time-Decay Principle places this in the medium-term window (4-10 years).  Consistent with that framework, individual evidence snippets warrant moderate scores (4-6) that acknowledge ongoing but diminished severity.  Mitigating specifics such as successful network agility programs or quantified cost offsets are largely absent, so no material downward adjustments apply beyond generic wording penalties.

evidence_list.snippet: The effects of a widespread outbreak of an illness or any other communicable disease or public health crisis on our business, results of operations, and financial condition are highly unpredictable.

components.reason: Explicitly links public-health crisis to business, operating and financial performance.
Highlights uncertainty ('highly unpredictable') which magnifies potential downside.
Generic, forward-looking wording without quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Directly identifies pandemic unpredictability as a material enterprise risk; no offsetting mitigations noted, yielding a moderate 5/10.

evidence_list.snippet: A widespread outbreak of an illness or any other communicable disease or public health crisis could have varying effects on the demand for our services, our business operations, and the global economy and supply chains.

components.reason: Names multiple impact channels: demand, operations, global economy, supply chains.
Conditional ('could') and unquantified statement.
Scope breadth signals elevated exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Enumerates several pandemic-driven impact vectors, but remains unquantified and conditional, landing at a moderate 4/10.

evidence_list.snippet: If we are unable to remain agile and flex our networks to align with shipping volumes, customer needs, disrupted global supply chains and other network inefficiencies, market demands, and operating conditions, or are unable to continuously respond to evolving governmental policies, our business operations could be negatively affected, which could have a further adverse effect on our results of operations.

components.reason: Identifies operational agility gap as a specific vulnerability during disruptions.
Directly ties failure to negative operational and financial outcomes.
Risk phrased as conditional possibility not current fact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Links supply-chain shocks from health crises to potential profit erosion, justifying a 4/10 score.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, due to the size, scope, and geographically dispersed nature of our operations, the expenses we incur to protect the health and safety of our team members and customers may be higher than similar expenses incurred by companies in other industries.

components.reason: Highlights cost pressure uniquely amplified by FDX’s scale and dispersion.
Uses comparative language ('higher than…other industries') indicating relative severity.
No mitigation or quantification provided.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Indicates structurally higher pandemic-related costs without offsets, earning 4/10.

evidence_list.snippet: To the extent a widespread outbreak of an illness or any other communicable disease or public health crisis adversely affects our business and financial results, it may also have the effect of heightening many other risks described in this section, any of which could materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, and financial condition.

components.reason: Warns of contagion effect—pandemic can amplify multiple other disclosed risks.
Uses strong materiality language ('materially and adversely affect').
Contingent phrasing and lack of metrics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Emphasises pandemic as a risk multiplier but stays hypothetical, resulting in 4/10.

evidence_list.snippet: A significant number of our employees as well as customers and others with whom we do business continue to work remotely or in hybrid models, which may heighten these risks.

components.reason: Connects pandemic-driven remote-work environment to elevated risk profile (e.g., cyber, operational).
Acknowledges current ongoing condition ('continue to work remotely').
Does not quantify impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows enduring remote-work exposure linked to pandemic, giving a moderate 4/10.

evidence_list.snippet: See “Item 1A. Risk Factors” and “Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Results of Operations and Financial Condition” of our Annual Reports on Form 10-K for the years ended May 31, 2020, May 31, 2021, May 31, 2022, and May 31, 2023 for information regarding the COVID-19 pandemic and its effects on our business, results of operations, and financial condition.

components.reason: Explicitly references prior COVID-19 impact disclosures, confirming historical materiality.
Merely cross-references past filings with no fresh detail—largely procedural.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Reference confirms pandemic relevance but adds no new risk detail, so minimal 1/10 score.
